title: CR-002 Song Corridor Editorial
description: Original living photographic fashion editorial informed by Song-dynasty Chinese visual culture: layered silk wardrobe, restrained hair, timber covered corridor staging, and soft architectural daylight. historically_informed (not strict reconstruction). Uses existing EraPack id song only; art.method null (photographic). Creative Research library entry; no gallery image attached. See docs/CR_002_SONG_CORRIDOR_EDITORIAL.md for sources and uncertainties.

semantic_spec.request: Create a quiet photographic fashion editorial of an adult woman standing in a Song-dynasty-informed timber covered corridor. Keep the result clearly photographic and living—not an ink painting, mural, costume-drama still, or fantasy xianxia tableau. Wardrobe is historically informed layered Song women’s dress: a straight-collar open-front beizi with long side slits over a slim ruqun (upper garment plus long skirt), light silk or silk-gauze with calm vertical drape. Hair is a restrained upswept bun with modest pin ornament only—no Tang tower bun, no Qing banner hairstyle, no ceremonial phoenix crown. Makeup is restrained with visible natural skin texture. Architecture shows a covered timber walkway with wooden columns, grey ceramic roof tiles, white plaster side wall, and an opening to a quiet courtyard garden that admits soft daylight. Prioritize layered spatial depth, material plausibility, and culturally coherent styling over spectacle.

body_transformation.anatomy_change: none; preserve natural adult proportions without idealizing measurements
body_transformation.pose_change: allowed as director-specified quiet editorial stance
body_transformation.garment_shaping: slim vertical Song-informed silhouette: open-front straight-collar beizi hanging in long vertical planes with underarm/side slits reading as construction, not costume flares; inner upper garment close to the torso; long skirt with soft columnar folds and slight hem weight; light silk/gauze layers that stack without ballooning; no floating scarves as wind FX
body_transformation.artistic_stylization: none; keep photographic material response (do not convert to ink, print, or mural grammar)

historical.subperiod: Southern Song-inspired restrained silhouette and quieter palette (not a dated reconstruction of a specific year)
historical.region: China; Jiangnan-inspired elite residential/garden corridor context

slim layered ruqun (upper garment and long skirt) in light silk or silk-gauze
restrained upswept bun with modest hairpin only
timber covered corridor with wooden columns and grey roof tiles
white plaster corridor wall and courtyard garden opening
soft daylight entering from architectural openings
layered foreground floor / midground figure / background corridor depth

director.moment: a brief pause mid-walk along the covered corridor, cloth settling after the last step
director.action: standing in a quiet three-quarter stance, one foot slightly advanced along the corridor axis, torso upright without parade stiffness
director.gaze: softly toward the courtyard opening rather than a hard camera stare; calm, unsmiling editorial attention
director.body_weight: front advanced foot carries primary weight; rear foot lightly grounded for recoverable balance
director.hand_logic: near hand rests lightly against the open beizi edge at mid-torso without clutching; far hand hangs relaxed along the skirt seam; no handheld props
director.fabric_response: outer beizi hangs in long vertical silk planes that part slightly at the open front; skirt layers show soft columnar folds with gentle gravity at the hem; gauze underlayers mute specular hotspots; no frozen wind flare
director.prop_interaction: no handheld props; optional quiet architectural contact only if a column is near—prefer free stance
director.foreground: tiled or beaten-earth corridor floor plane with soft shadow falloff toward the viewer
director.midground: full-length adult subject reading as one slim vertical silhouette inside the column rhythm
director.background: receding timber covered corridor with white plaster wall, grey tiled roof underside, and a bright-quiet courtyard garden opening beyond
director.camera: eye-level three-quarter full-length editorial frame aligned to the corridor axis with slight subject offset from center
director.light_source: soft daylight from the courtyard-side corridor openings as key, large and diffuse, gentle fill from plaster bounce, restrained contrast without cinematic god-rays
director.material_response: silk and silk-gauze show quiet directional sheen along fold crowns; timber columns read as matte wood grain; plaster absorbs light; skin and hair remain photographic rather than painterly
director.micro_story: a private pause between rooms—architectural calm translated into a still editorial beat
